description: Soft pins for known-open defects. Every expect_fail case here asserts the behaviour that is CORRECT per the documentation or the engine's own stated doctrine, and is expected to fail until the defect is fixed — the runner reports it without going red, and a PASS fails the gate so the fixing commit must promote the case (and tighten its assert where the fix settles a shape this case had to leave open). Each expect_fail travels with a control on the same fixture, so corpus drift or an unregistered corpus fails a control loudly instead of masquerading as the expected failure.

cases.name: control_the_lines_clause_target_exists
cases.description: Anchors the parse case below: the function the multi-step case reads is present and unique in the fixture.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'controlFlowPatterns' IN 'tests/fixtures/enrichment_patterns.cpp'

cases.name: the_advertised_lines_clause_parses_on_show_node
cases.description: SHOW NODE advertises a lines_clause — the parse error for LINES 2-4 itself lists lines_clause as expected — but the range form, the exact syntax the standalone SHOW LINES statement uses, fails to parse at the hyphen. The node-relative suffix '<id>(n-m)' covers the need, but a clause the grammar advertises should parse, or the error should state the shape it does accept.
cases.expect_fail_reason: SHOW NODE '<id>' LINES A-B is a parse error while SHOW LINES A-B OF '<file>' works, and the error message lists lines_clause among the expected clauses, which is actively misleading; when the grammar accepts the form, promote this case and pin the returned rows

cases.name: control_scoped_variables_share_one_name_count
cases.description: Anchors the case below and records the defect's shape: ten let-bindings named session_id, in ten different test files, every one reporting the identical usages value of 236 — the corpus-wide count of the NAME, not references to any binding. The assertion that pinned that shape (all_same on usages) cannot survive the fix and was replaced here rather than kept: once no row carries the field, all_same over an absent key is satisfied by every result, an empty one included, so it would have gone on passing while proving nothing. What this control anchors now is the fixture — ten rows, every one a local-scope variable — and the absence itself is pinned by the case below.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'session_id' WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE scope = 'local' IN 'crates/forgeql-core/tests/**'

cases.name: a_local_variables_usages_is_not_a_corpus_wide_name_count
cases.description: PROMOTED. `usages` is the workspace-total count of a NAME's role='code' occurrence sites, which is a real dependency count only where the name identifies the symbol across the workspace. A local binding's name identifies nothing outside its block — the engine does not resolve scoped references — so every one of these ten rows reported 236, and the blast-radius workflow the agent docs teach (ORDER BY usages DESC) read that as references. A local-scope variable now carries NO usages value at all. row_count is asserted alongside the pointers so the absence cannot be satisfied by an empty result: /results/0/usages is null on a zero-row answer too, and that is exactly how this pin could pass while proving nothing. The last row is pinned as well as the first, so a suppression that reached only part of the answer would be caught.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'session_id' WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE scope = 'local' IN 'crates/forgeql-core/tests/**'

cases.name: control_a_long_literal_groups_by_file_correctly
cases.description: Anchors the cases below. A name PATTERN is not counted from the index -- no pattern tier verifies the candidates it proposes -- so this grouping is answered by the scan, and the 57 files it reports are the files that hold a matching row. The counted route used to answer this shape and happened to agree here, which is exactly why the cases below exist: agreement was the corpus being kind, not the path being exact. The line pins the route, since a counted group row from this path carries none of its own.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name LIKE '%segment%' GROUP BY file ORDER BY count DESC

cases.name: control_the_scan_counts_the_short_literal
cases.description: The authoritative answer the case below asserts, taken through the scan: adding a predicate the file fast path does not admit (line >= 0, which holds for every row and removes nothing) sends the same grouping to the pipeline, where each row's own name decides. 165 files hold a symbol whose name contains 'ab'; CHANGELOG.md holds 533 of them.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE line >= 0 WHERE name LIKE '%ab%' GROUP BY file ORDER BY count DESC

cases.name: a_counted_group_by_file_counts_only_matching_rows
cases.description: A GROUP BY file counted from the index returns the counts the scan returns. A name PATTERN is not one of the shapes it counts: the trigram tier over-generates by construction, and below its literal width it declines outright, leaving every row of a file a candidate and every candidate a count. group_by_file_fast_path_eligible hands the pattern to the scan, which decides each row by reading it. The line: 3 pins that route -- a counted group row carries no line of its own. The two shapes that ARE counted, fql_kind = and name =, are served by postings intersected with the canonical rows at build; this one has no such structure to be served from.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name LIKE '%ab%' GROUP BY file ORDER BY count DESC

cases.name: control_a_kind_predicate_groups_by_file_exactly
cases.description: Anchors the case below by isolating the one admitted predicate, through the SCAN. The kind postings ARE intersected with each segment's canonical row set at overlay build (step5_build_kind_postings, with the comment saying so), so a fql_kind = predicate beside GROUP BY file counts each row once. Its counted twin is the next case; the two agreeing is the claim, and a control that ran the counted route alone could not have made it.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE line >= 0 WHERE fql_kind = 'number' IN 'crates/forgeql-core/src/transforms/diff.rs' GROUP BY file

cases.name: a_counted_group_by_file_still_counts_a_kind_predicate
cases.description: The twin, and the reason the fix is not simply to decline everything: fql_kind = stays on the counted route and reaches the control's 215 without materialising a row. The empty name and zero line are what say it stayed -- the scan's row for this group carries a name of its own. Without this case, a later change that declined this shape too would leave every other case in this file green while the counted path quietly died.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'number' IN 'crates/forgeql-core/src/transforms/diff.rs' GROUP BY file

cases.name: control_the_scan_counts_each_name_once
cases.description: The authoritative answer the case below asserts. This file holds 48 rows named '0'; the row listing returns 48 of them, and the scan's grouping counts 48.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE line >= 0 WHERE name = '0' IN 'crates/forgeql-core/src/transforms/diff.rs' GROUP BY file

cases.name: a_counted_group_by_file_counts_each_row_once
cases.description: The half of the defect that needed no pattern, only a plain name equality -- the shape the old eligibility rule most obviously intended to admit, and the one it could not count. step6_build_name_fst merged each segment's RAW name postings into the overlay FST without the canonical intersection that step5_build_kind_postings and collect_posting_enrichment both apply, so a name posting carried the intra-segment duplicates the answer collapses: this file reported 57 rows named '0' where it holds 48. The intersection now runs at overlay build, which is what makes a name equality countable and re-admits it here. The count is the control's 48, and the empty name and zero line are what say the counted route reached it -- the scan's row for this group carries a name of its own, at line 191.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = '0' IN 'crates/forgeql-core/src/transforms/diff.rs' GROUP BY file

cases.name: control_the_scan_counts_an_answered_pattern
cases.description: The authoritative answer for the case below: 768 rows of this file carry a name containing 'name'. The literal is four bytes, so the trigram tier answers it rather than declining — this is not the sub-trigram shape.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE line >= 0 WHERE name LIKE '%name%' IN 'crates/forgeql/tests/golden.json' GROUP BY file

cases.name: a_counted_group_by_file_counts_an_answered_pattern_once
cases.description: The case that said there is no safe literal length for a PATTERN. This four-byte pattern IS served by the trigram index, and the counted grouping still came back one row high -- because a tier that answers still only proposes, and nothing tested a proposal against its own row. It is kept beside the sub-trigram case so neither is read as marking a boundary the other stays inside: what settles a name predicate is not the length of its literal, it is whether the structure serving it was intersected with the canonical rows at build. The name FST now is, so a name EQUALITY is counted; the trigram index is not and cannot be, since it over-generates by construction, so every name pattern stays with the scan at every length.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name LIKE '%name%' IN 'crates/forgeql/tests/golden.json' GROUP BY file

cases.name: control_the_scan_answers_a_having_on_a_row_field
cases.description: Anchors the two cases below. HAVING runs after the grouping pass, over whatever the retained row carries. On the scan that row is the first row of its group, so HAVING lines >= 2 keeps the six kinds whose representative is a multi-line node.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE line >= 0 GROUP BY fql_kind HAVING lines >= 2

cases.name: a_counted_group_by_fql_kind_answers_a_having_on_a_row_field
cases.description: A HAVING the counted route cannot evaluate sends the query back to the scan rather than answering nothing. It used to build SymbolMatch rows carrying only name/fql_kind/count and run the HAVING over them, so a predicate naming any other field was false on every group and the empty set came back with full confidence -- 0 rows where the scan returns 6. group_by_kind_fast_path_eligible now asks only_the_group_row_is_read first, the same test group_by_enrichment_fast_path_field already applied. The struct row pins that the scan answered: a counted group row carries no line of its own.
cases.fql: FIND symbols GROUP BY fql_kind HAVING lines >= 2

cases.name: control_the_scan_answers_a_having_on_a_row_field_grouped_by_file
cases.description: The same anchor for the file grouping: three files whose retained row is a multi-line node.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE line >= 0 GROUP BY file HAVING lines >= 2

cases.name: a_counted_group_by_file_answers_a_having_on_a_row_field
cases.description: The file grouping's half of the same contract, pinned separately because the two eligibility functions are separate and a fix could land on one before the other. It handed apply_clauses_counted rows carrying only path and count, so HAVING lines >= 2 was false on every group and 0 rows came back where the scan returns 3. The named row pins the route: a counted group row from this path carries an empty name.
cases.fql: FIND symbols GROUP BY file HAVING lines >= 2

cases.name: control_zephyr_locals_share_one_name_count
cases.description: Anchors the case below at corpus scale and records the defect's shape there: 11,964 local bindings named ret, every row carrying the identical corpus-wide count of the NAME (83,611). Verified live 2026-08-24 on 0.183.0. As with its forgeql-pub twin, the all_same-on-usages assertion this control carried is vacuous once no row carries the field, so it anchors the fixture instead — three rows, every one a local-scope variable — and the absence is pinned below.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'ret' WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE scope = 'local' LIMIT 3

cases.name: a_local_usages_is_not_a_name_count_on_zephyr
cases.description: PROMOTED. The forgeql-pub case pins ten session_id bindings; this pins the same rule where it hurt most — ret, the most reused local name in C, where 83,611 is not merely wrong but absurd, and the blast-radius recipe in every agent doc would have read it as real references. row_count is asserted with the pointers because a zero-row answer also yields null at /results/0/usages.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'ret' WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE scope = 'local' LIMIT 3

cases.name: control_a_file_scope_variable_keeps_its_usage_count
cases.description: The other half of the ruling, and the reason the suppression is written as fql_kind='variable' AND scope='local' rather than as 'variables have no usage count'. A FILE-scope variable's name does identify it across the workspace, so its count is real and must not move: ENRICH_VER is referenced 13 times on this corpus, before the fix and after. Widen the suppression to file scope — the obvious over-reach — and this control goes red while every local pin stays green, which is the mutation check that says the boundary is where the ruling put it.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'ENRICH_VER' WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE scope = 'file'

cases.name: control_a_function_keeps_its_usage_count
cases.description: The same guard for the row kind the hotspot recipe is actually about. A function is never suppressed, so its count must read exactly as it did before: populate_usage_counts is referenced 3 times on this corpus. A suppression keyed on scope alone rather than on scope AND kind would take this row too, since the scope enricher writes 'local' on any declaration node inside a function body.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'populate_usage_counts' WHERE fql_kind = 'function'

cases.name: control_the_zephyr_file_scope_variable_keeps_its_count
cases.description: The file-scope guard at corpus scale: dev, the most reused file-scope name on this corpus, keeps its 98,605 while the 11,964 local ret rows lose theirs. Without it, a suppression that leaked to every variable would leave the two local pins above green and nothing red.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'dev' WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE scope = 'file' LIMIT 3

cases.name: control_a_zephyr_function_keeps_its_usage_count
cases.description: The function guard at corpus scale. z_impl_k_sleep is declared twice on this corpus and both rows report 3, unchanged by the suppression.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = 'z_impl_k_sleep' WHERE fql_kind = 'function'

cases.name: a_local_variable_cannot_be_ranked_by_a_usage_count_it_does_not_have
cases.description: The hotspot recipe the agent docs teach, aimed at the row kind that used to poison it. Before, the top of this ranking was three local bindings named new in transforms/diff.rs, each reporting 1,544 — the corpus-wide count of the name. After, a row with no value ranks behind every row that has one, in both directions, so the page is the file-scope variables whose counts are real. The language is pinned to rust because every scope-less variable row on this corpus is a C++ parameter that keeps its name count (see the case below), and this pin is about the ordering, not about that residual. The ordering half of the fix is not free: the comparator takes its numeric branch only when BOTH rows answer with a number, and its string fallback reads nothing on either side for a field the row type declares numeric — so without the new arm a local and a file-scope variable compared EQUAL and a name/line tie-break decided the page, which is a worse answer than the one it replaced.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE language = 'rust' ORDER BY usages DESC LIMIT 3

cases.name: a_cpp_parameter_still_carries_its_names_corpus_count
cases.description: PINS CURRENT BEHAVIOUR, NOT THE DESIRED ANSWER — promote it when the gap closes. The ruling suppresses `usages` on a variable row whose `scope` enrichment reads `local`, and deliberately not on a variable row carrying no `scope` at all: the enricher writes the field only on nodes its language declares a declaration kind, so an unexamined row is not a row known to be local, and inventing an absence there would hide counts that are real. On this corpus that boundary has exactly one population — 157 C++ function PARAMETERS, every scope-less variable row here — and a parameter is as local as any binding: `int len` in `void rangeForLoop(int arr[], int len)` still reports 745, the corpus-wide count of the name `len`, while the 11 rust `let len` bindings report nothing. Closing it means teaching the scope enricher about parameter declarations, which changes index output and needs its own enrichment-version bump; this case asserts the CURRENT number so that the day it closes, it goes red and this text is read.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE name = 'len' IN 'tests/fixtures/enrichment_patterns.cpp'

cases.name: a_local_variable_matches_no_numeric_usages_predicate
cases.description: The WHERE half. 105 rows on this corpus answered fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE usages > 1000, every one a local binding carrying its name's corpus-wide count; the highest count any file-scope variable here carries is 264, so the honest answer is none. A row with no value for a field matches no numeric predicate on it — including usages = 0, which is why the dead-code recipe no longer sweeps every local into its result.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'variable' WHERE usages > 1000

cases.name: a_usages_predicate_answers_the_same_on_show_body_as_on_find
cases.description: Found while enumerating every reader of the column, and fixed with the rest: the symbol-resolution path that serves SHOW body/signature/outline/members mapped a usages predicate onto the per-segment usages_count column — a stale always-zero legacy field — in its zone-map prune, and then evaluated the predicate against a row it had never stamped. Both halves said zero, so WHERE usages > 0 answered 'no symbol matches' for a symbol FIND reports 3 usages for, and WHERE usages = 0 matched every symbol. The prune now skips the field exactly as the FIND path always did, and the candidate row is stamped before the predicate reads it. The control above pins the number this must agree with.
cases.fql: SHOW body OF 'populate_usage_counts' DEPTH 0 WHERE usages > 0

cases.name: control_line_463_is_still_the_subscript
cases.description: Anchors the identity of the line, not just the row: the pin below is addressed by line number against a frozen snapshot, so a re-pin that shifts the fixture could put an `int x = 0;` declaration on 463 and turn the pin green while proving nothing.
cases.fql: SHOW LINES 463-463 OF 'tests/fixtures/enrichment_patterns.cpp' WHERE text MATCHES 'arr\[0\] = 1'

cases.name: control_the_fixture_holds_its_subscript_zero
cases.description: Anchors the case below: `arr[0] = 1;` at line 463 of the C++ fixture is indexed as a number row at all. If this control moves, the fixture changed, not the exemption.
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'tests/fixtures/enrichment_patterns.cpp' WHERE fql_kind = 'number' WHERE name = '0' WHERE line = 463 LIMIT 5

cases.name: a_zero_array_subscript_is_exempt_in_cpp
cases.description: The documented exemption for `arr[0]` does not fire on a C++ file. tree-sitter-cpp wraps a subscript index in a `subscript_argument_list`, so the literal's parent is that node and never the `subscript_expression` the enricher compares against. Every other grammar that declares a subscript kind names the index as a direct child, so the rule works in C, Rust and Python — it is the C++ grammar that is the exception, and it also claims `.h`, `.hpp` and the rest. Verified live 2026-08-25 on 0.185.0.
cases.expect_fail_reason: the zero-subscript exemption is dead under the C++ grammar — the enricher matches the parent kind against the configured subscript node while that grammar interposes `subscript_argument_list`; it fires correctly in C, Rust and Python, whose grammars name the index as a direct child. The unit test meant to cover this asserted only a non-empty result, which the fixture's `int x = 0;` declarations satisfied on their own, so nothing reported the dead branch. Fixing it changes index output and needs an enrichment version bump.
cases.fql: FIND symbols IN 'tests/fixtures/enrichment_patterns.cpp' WHERE fql_kind = 'number' WHERE name = '0' WHERE line = 463 WHERE is_magic = 'false' LIMIT 5
